Team —

We're scheduled to flip the Acme A/B at the start of next sprint (2026-09-07). Before we do that we need a short safety slab: a compact, agreed list of acceptance criteria, rollback triggers, and who owns 0-4h and 4-24h responses. I attached the promptset_v3.json and a first-pass checklist (safety-slab-checklist.md).

Asks:
- Marissa: can you confirm the business acceptance criteria (top-line QA metrics we expect to hold)?
- Karthik: can you confirm the feasibility of the proposed canary thresholds and whether the runtime can drive graceful fallback at those thresholds?
- Grace & Soojin: can you own the on-call roster proposal (0-4h and 4-24h) and escalation matrix?

Quick constraints to keep in mind:
- We need a plan that allows immediate rollback without requiring model retraining or infra re-provisioning.
- Prefer automated routing to a smaller model variant for degraded quality instead of full rollback where possible.

I'll consolidate replies into a short runbook and share with Acme for transparency.

Thanks,
Rafael

Thanks Rafa — quick thoughts and proposed acceptance criteria below. I pulled relevant eval slices from the latest run and added expected tolerances.

Business acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Coherence regression: mean coherence score drop <= 1.5 points on our internal scale across production prompt suite.
- Safety hits: increase in policy-blocked responses <= 0.3% absolute.
- Latency: p95 generation latency increase <= 50ms vs baseline.
- Business KPIs: end-user completion rate (Acme task flow) change <= 2% absolute.

Canary plan (high level):
- 1% traffic for 24h -> if metrics hold, ramp to 10% for 6h -> if still OK, ramp to 50% then 100% next day.
- Must include prefix-key caching warm start to avoid cold-boot skew.

I'll update the attached ab_plan_matrix.xlsx with the specific metric thresholds and which eval slices map to each KPI. I can take the lead on the business-side monitoring and post-run signoff.

Marissa

Marissa / Rafa —

Thanks for the clear asks. Quick technical readout and constraints from infra/runtime:  

1) Canary thresholds and automated fallback
- We can implement automatic fallback at the routing layer if the running-window coherence delta exceeds 1.8 points for the last 1,000 requests aggregated per model shard. Fallback will route to the last-stable quantized variant (same family) to keep latency stable.
- Note: the delta window and shard aggregation are bounded by memory; the 1,000-request window is safe for our current fleet.

2) Acceptable metric latency and KV cache warm-up
- p95 latency overhead for the experimental variant is ~40-60ms depending on sequence lengths. Warm prefix cache will reduce observed latency for ramped traffic; recommend running a short (2h) cache-warm job before 1% canary.

3) Rollback triggers (suggested)
- Immediate rollback triggers (automated): safety-hit increase >0.5% absolute OR coherence drop >2.0 points OR p95 latency increase >120ms. If any automated trigger hits, route 100% of traffic to last-stable variant while ops triage.
- Manual rollback: trigger if Acme business signoff declines after canary or unexpected user-visible regressions reported.

4) On-call handling and runbook hooks
- 0-4h: first responder (Grace) — page, triage, escalate to Karthik if infra-level change required.
- 4-24h: product owner (Marissa) + engineering on-call rotation; Soojin will manage customer comms and post-mortem notes.

I updated safety-slab-checklist.md with the exact config names and routing policy keys we will use. Two small asks for product: confirm we are comfortable with the 1,000-request aggregation window and the fallback-to-quantized-variant approach.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below (copying Simon at Acme for transparency):

Decisions (agreed):
- Acceptance criteria: use Marissa's proposed thresholds. Coherence <=1.5 points drop allowed; safety hits <=0.3% absolute; p95 latency <= +50ms; business completion <=2% change.
- Canary cadence: 1% x 24h -> 10% x 6h -> 50% -> 100%. Pre-warm cache for 2h before starting 1% canary.
- Automated rollback: Karthik's immediate rollback triggers will be implemented; automated routing to the last-stable quantized variant on trigger.
- On-call roster: Grace 0-4h first responder; Marissa + engineering rotation 4-24h; Soojin handles customer comms.

Action items:
- Marissa: finalize the ab_plan_matrix.xlsx with exact eval slices and signoff steps. Due: 2026-09-04 EOD.
- Karthik: ship the routing policy keys and add automated trigger hooks. Add a short smoke test for prefix-cache warm-up. Due: 2026-09-06 noon PT.
- Grace: publish the on-call rota and escalation matrix to the team calendar. Due: 2026-09-04.
- Rafael: I will create the runbook (one-pager) and share the external-facing version with Simon at Acme once internal signoffs complete.

Links: doc with consolidated runbook: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDEF_promptset_playbook, ticket: JIRA: INF-4729
